head.citation-title: Recycling of steel slag and water-quenched slag into a cement-free cementitious material via accelerated carbonation curing: its CO2capture prediction model, mechanical properties, microstructural development, and photocatalytic outcome
head.abstracts: © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.A cement-free cementitious material composed of steel slag (SS) and water-quenched slag (WQS) was successfully developed via accelerated carbonation curing. The experimental results demonstrated that the XRD and FTIR analyses revealed that, in addition to the carbonation of portlandite (CH), dicalcium silicate (C2S), and tricalcium silicate (C3S), the carbonation of tricalcium aluminate (C3A) and brownmillerite (C4AF), along with the decalcification of calcium silicate hydrate, significantly enhanced CO2 capture, mechanical properties, and microstructure, which was also confirmed by the SEM-EDS and MIP results, while the photocatalytic activity of perovskite in WQS was responsible for pollutant degradation. Based on these findings, an accurate mathematical model for CO2 capture was proposed, incorporating the carbonation reactions of CH, C2S, C3S, C3A, and C4AF, and an optimal mix ratio considering both carbon capture and photocatalytic outcome was proposed, which holds promise for use in sustainable construction practice (i.e., sewage treatment plants and outdoor drainage channels).

coredata.dc:description: A cement-free cementitious material composed of steel slag (SS) and water-quenched slag (WQS) was successfully developed via accelerated carbonation curing. The experimental results demonstrated that the XRD and FTIR analyses revealed that, in addition to the carbonation of portlandite (CH), dicalcium silicate (C2S), and tricalcium silicate (C3S), the carbonation of tricalcium aluminate (C3A) and brownmillerite (C4AF), along with the decalcification of calcium silicate hydrate, significantly enhanced CO2 capture, mechanical properties, and microstructure, which was also confirmed by the SEM-EDS and MIP results, while the photocatalytic activity of perovskite in WQS was responsible for pollutant degradation. Based on these findings, an accurate mathematical model for CO2 capture was proposed, incorporating the carbonation reactions of CH, C2S, C3S, C3A, and C4AF, and an optimal mix ratio considering both carbon capture and photocatalytic outcome was proposed, which holds promise for use in sustainable construction practice (i.e., sewage treatment plants and outdoor drainage channels).
coredata.dc:title: Recycling of steel slag and water-quenched slag into a cement-free cementitious material via accelerated carbonation curing: its CO2capture prediction model, mechanical properties, microstructural development, and photocatalytic outcome
